answer.answer: On average, about 3.52 days pass between a customer's first order and their second order.
answer.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT customer_id, ordered_at::date AS order_date,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at) AS rn
  FROM main.orders
), first_second AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN order_date END) AS first_order_date,
         MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN order_date END) AS second_order_date,
         COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM ordered
  WHERE rn IN (1,2)
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
)
SELECT AVG(date_diff('day', first_order_date, second_order_date)) AS avg_days_between_first_and_second
FROM first_second;
answer.definition_used: Average number of days between the first and second order dates for customers who have placed at least two orders.

answer.answer: The Brooklyn store drove the jump – it had 0 orders in February 2025 and 2,017 orders in March 2025, accounting for the bulk of the near‑doubling.
answer.sql:
SELECT l.location_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS feb_orders,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mar_orders,
       (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -
        SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS diff
FROM main.orders o
JOIN main.locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.ordered_at)=2025
GROUP BY l.location_name
ORDER BY diff DESC
LIMIT 1;
answer.definition_used: Count of orders per store for February (month=2) and March (month=3) 2025; the store with the largest increase (difference) explains the jump.

steps.sql:
SELECT l.location_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at) = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS feb_orders,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at) = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mar_orders,
       (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at) = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -
        SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at) = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS diff
FROM main.orders o
JOIN main.locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.ordered_at) = 2025
GROUP BY l.location_name
ORDER BY diff DESC
LIMIT 1

SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ordered_at)=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS feb_total,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ordered_at)=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mar_total
FROM main.orders
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ordered_at)=2025

SELECT l.location_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS feb_orders,
       SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ordered_at)=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mar_orders
FROM main.orders o
JOIN main.locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.ordered_at)=2025
GROUP BY l.location_name
ORDER BY mar_orders DESC

steps.text:
The surge is driven almost entirely by the **Brooklyn** store.  

- In February 2025 the Brooklyn location recorded **0 orders**.  
- In March 2025 it recorded **2,017 orders**.  

Overall orders grew from 3,446 in February to 6,181 in March (≈ 79 % increase). The jump is explained by the Brooklyn store’s sudden activity, accounting for the bulk of the increase.
